name: Kemuel
title: Nahor's son and Aram's father
summary: Kemuel was a son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his wife Milcah. He is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Aram. The name Kemuel also appears in other contexts in the Old Testament, including as a leader from the tribe of Ephraim and as a Levitical leader.

siblings: Maacah, son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah

keyEvents.title: The birth of Kemuel is mentioned
keyEvents.description: After the binding of Isaac, Abraham learned that his brother Nahor had several sons with his wife Milcah, including Kemuel, who became the father of Aram.

keyEvents.title: Kemuel's family connection to Abraham
keyEvents.description: Kemuel is connected to Abraham's extended family through his father Nahor, who was Abraham's brother. This family link was important in Israel's patriarchal history.

keyEvents.title: Kemuel as father of Aram
keyEvents.description: Kemuel is identified as the father of Aram, linking him to the Arameans and the broader Semitic peoples in Mesopotamia.

keyEvents.title: Another Kemuel as a leader in Ephraim
keyEvents.description: A man named Kemuel, son of Shuham, was appointed as a leader for the tribe of Ephraim to help distribute the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Kemuel as a Levitical leader
keyEvents.description: In David's time, a Kemuel, son of Hashabiah, is mentioned as a leader over the Levites, showing that the name held significance across several generations in Israel's history.
